input.code:
def process(water2020, water2021, water2022, water2023):
    import pandas as pd

    def prep(df: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
        out = df.copy()
        out = out[out['Beach Type Description'].astype(str).str.strip().str.lower() == 'fresh']
        # Normalize Violation to boolean: YES/Yes => True, else False
        v = out['Violation'].astype(str).str.strip().str.upper()
        out['exceed'] = v.eq('YES')
        return out[['Year', 'Beach Name', 'exceed']]

    d2020 = prep(water2020)
    d2021 = prep(water2021)
    d2022 = prep(water2022)
    d2023 = prep(water2023)

    # Beaches measured in all years (set intersection)
    common = set(d2020['Beach Name'].unique())
    for d in (d2021, d2022, d2023):
        common &= set(d['Beach Name'].unique())

    allData = pd.concat([d2020, d2021, d2022, d2023], ignore_index=True)
    allData = allData[allData['Beach Name'].isin(common)]

    rates = (
        allData.groupby('Beach Name', as_index=False)
        .agg(avgExceedanceRate=('exceed', 'mean'), nSamples=('exceed', 'size'))
        .sort_values(['avgExceedanceRate', 'nSamples', 'Beach Name'], ascending=[False, False, True])
    )

    return rates.head(1)
input.summary: Compute most polluted fresh-water beach across 2020-2023: filter each yearly table to Beach Type Description == 'Fresh' (case-insensitive); normalize Violation to exceed boolean (YES/Yes->True, otherwise False); take intersection of Beach Name values present in all four years; concatenate 2020-2023 and, for common beaches only, groupby Beach Name to compute avgExceedanceRate=mean(exceed) and nSamples=count; sort by avgExceedanceRate desc, then nSamples desc, then Beach Name asc; return top 1 beach.
